short: The first authorised edition of the Bible in English was published for use in church services.
full:
In April 1539, the Great Bible was issued as the first official English translation of the scriptures, heavily championed by Thomas Cromwell and meticulously prepared by Myles Coverdale. King Henry VIII commanded by royal injunction that a copy of this large, expensive folio Bible be permanently chained to a reading desk in every parish church in England, accessible to all parishioners.

The publication marked a profound and irreversible shift in English religious culture, breaking the ancient clerical monopoly on scripture and making the biblical text widely available in the vernacular. Although Henry later grew anxious about lay interpretation and restricted lower-class access, the Great Bible laid the textual foundation for later influential translations and vastly accelerated the spread of Protestant theology.
